newsitem.title: USA: US MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS SEEN STEADY-OFF $1 - DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: US MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS SEEN STEADY-OFF $1 - DEALERS.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt lower on outlooks for continued hefty marketings, livestock dealers said. Marketings the past two days have overshadowed light to moderate demand, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog receipts Monday totalled 108,000 head, versus the estimate of 100,000, USDA reported. Tuesday's estimate was 100,000 head.
"We're getting big runs and the weights are right where they should be," an Indiana hog dealer said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were seen steady at $57.50, sources there said. Illinois top prices at plants were expected steady to $0.50 lower at $56.00 to $56.50, Illinois sources said.

Indiana/Ohio hog prices at the plant were seen down $1.00, with a top of $56.00. Top hog prices Tuesday at plants in the Indiana/Ohio market were unevenly steady, with the bulk at $57.00 and a few at $57.25, USDA reported.
Declines could be tempered by firm demand from some packers who have been able to maintain profitable operating margins despite lower pork prices Monday, buyers said.
